quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.text: Indeed, only in Sumeru can you truly feel nature. The air in Fontaine, by contrast, is practically toxic fumes...
What is it? Can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're just a bit curious.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you live in this tent?
Yes, I've been living here for a while now. Oh, I get it... It's weird to see someone from Fontaine living in a tent out in the Sumeru wilds, eh?
As for why... I shall explain. But first, what are your names?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's name is Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.
#So, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Noted.

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: I'm Santon. As you can see, I'm from Fontaine, and I'm here in Sumeru for the forest, of course! I love forests!

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: If you live in the city for too long, your body grows weak from the lack of exercise and your mind grows complacent.

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: Only in the vast expanse of the outdoors can you regain any sense of harmony. Forests are the best place to get re-connected to nature.

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: That's why I came to Sumeru. After all, the forests here are probably the best in Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon kinda understands, but also not really...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But with all the kinds of monsters present in them, the forests of Sumeru can be pretty dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: That's the point!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: I wouldn't feel the thrill if there was no danger at all! Worry not, I'm actually a famous hunter in Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, it's hunting in the forests that you're actually in love with!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're just a poacher from Fontaine, aren't you!?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: No, you've got it wrong. I'm no poacher! Poaching is a serious crime!

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: If you get caught poaching in Fontaine, your life is over. I'd never dare to do that. We Fontaine hunters deal mostly with "fierce animals."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Deal with fierce animals?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Think about it. Fierce animals coming too close to human settlements do harm to both sides, so they have to be kept away from human dwellings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what you do...?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Yeah, this way, those who live nearby will no longer be disturbed by ferocious animals, and conversely, human activities will also cease to trouble the animals.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: To be honest, I had heard that there were some fierce animals in the vicinity, and I was hired to drive them away. I mean, as a hunter, how could I sit by, right?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Of course, I do have an interest in such creatures myself.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: That overgrown gator is pretty impressive, for instance. Known to kids as the "Gator Raja," it sounds like it came straight out of an urban legend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Overgrown crocodile? Could that be the one we met before, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: You drove the legendary Gator Raja away?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: It is said that the Gator Raja is akin to an emerging giant sandbar as it rises from rushing river current, and is even capable of cutting the river's flow off! Is that true?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Amazing!

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: I thought I felt the vibe of seasoned hunters off you guys. Guess I wasn't mistaken!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course not, we've been through a lot of adventures together.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Other than the Gator Raja, there are two beasts out there — one is the Rishboland Raja that steals children and the other is the huge Sumpter Beast that blocks the passage to Liyue...

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: The Rishboland Raja seems to be in the jungle west of here.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: It is said that the Sumpter Beastlord is an incomparably large Sumpter Beast... Several frightened witnesses have claimed that it haunts the east, assaulting unfortunate passersby.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They sound pretty dangerous...

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Yes. Be careful when you see them. But if you handled the Gator Raja, perhaps my concerns are unnecessary.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: If you happen to run into them, please drive them away!

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: That should keep the people here safe!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure, if we do come across them.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: I'd appreciate it!

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Please take heed of the safety of the people, the ferocious animals and of course, yourselves!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it!

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Is that so? I find that somewhat disappointing, somehow...

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Ordinary crocodiles are already tough to handle, so dealing with the devious Gator Raja must be a truly perilous endeavor.

response.speaker: Santon

response.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: So, did you run into any of those ferocious creatures?

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: If you happen to encounter the creatures, please drive them away. It would be a good thing, for people and animals both.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: They say that the Gator Raja haunts the waters on the east side of the city. But I've checked several times and have never seen the cunning beast.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: The story around here is that the Rishboland Raja comes out of the forest in the west at midnight and snatches naughty kids who aren't willing to go to bed.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Parents probably made up the kidnapping part to scare their kids to bed, but Rishboland Tigers are indeed more active at night.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Rumor has it that some wayfarers traveling at night were chased by a huge Rishboland tiger, though fortunately, there have been no casualties thus far.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: I've heard that some wild Sumpter Beasts are territorial and will attack intruders. I'm sure the Sumpter Beastlord is the same.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Its turf is somewhere in the east.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: I wonder just how big the Sumpter Beastlord must be to have earned that moniker.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Well, keep up the good work!

dialogues.speaker: Hong
dialogues.text: The "Sumpter Beastlord"? That was a few days ago. I was looking for some special ore, and somehow ended up on the other side of the mountain...

dialogues.speaker: Hong
dialogues.text: And there was the huge Sumpter Beast. Gee. It was so huge. I've never seen such a huge one in my life.

dialogues.speaker: Hong
dialogues.text: It charged toward me the moment it saw me. Luckily, I ran fast enough to escape...

dialogues.speaker: Hong
dialogues.text: The other side of which mountain? Ah, it's one of the mountains to the west. I can't remember more details... But it must be one of the peaks to the west.

dialogues.speaker: Najib
dialogues.text: The Sumpter Beastlord? You mean the giant Sumpter Beast, right?

dialogues.speaker: Najib
dialogues.text: I was going over to Liyue two days ago when I saw it by The Chasm.

dialogues.speaker: Najib
dialogues.text: Luckily for me, it was napping. I tiptoed around and got away. It was the size of a hill.

dialogues.speaker: Najib
dialogues.text: Where did I see it? Liyue is to the south from here, so it must be somewhere down in that direction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But don't people usually travel to Liyue from Sumeru by water? Why even go near The Chasm?

dialogues.speaker: Najib
dialogues.text: That's rather... personal. It has nothing to do with you, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Najib
dialogues.text: And that's all I know. I've got other things to do, so leave me alone!

dialogues.speaker: Anaya
dialogues.text: The "Sumpter Beastlord"? I saw it when I was in the forest the other night.

dialogues.speaker: Anaya
dialogues.text: It was a cloudy night. I was walking when a shadow of the size of a mound rushed toward me with a rumbling sound...

dialogues.speaker: Anaya
dialogues.text: I fainted. And I came to myself the next day. The guy who carried me back said I collapsed at the foot of the mountain. Luckily I was not seriously injured...

dialogues.speaker: Anaya
dialogues.text: Well, I'm not so sure about the exact location... Maybe it's in the east...

dialogues.speaker: A Notice
dialogues.text: "About the recent sightings of large Rishboland Tigers:"

dialogues.speaker: A Notice
dialogues.text: "Please do not loiter after dark. The Rishboland Tigers are known to come out at night."

dialogues.speaker: A Notice
dialogues.text: "Please do not leave any meat in this area. Feeding the tigers is not the correct way to stay safe. Conversely, it may encourage the tigers to stay."

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: You've driven the savage creatures away?

dialogues.speaker: Santon
dialogues.text: I haven't even seen any yet. So, how fearsome were those creatures?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Sounds like it was a cakewalk for you.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: I'm relieved to know those creatures are gone, though I'm bitter that I didn't get to see them.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: It's common to see stronger predators beat their rivals to the prey...

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Haha, but I won't lose next time!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're not going to lose to you, either!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But isn't "handling fierce animals" supposedly the duty of the Forest Rangers here in Sumeru?

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Huh? Didn't I say so before? This is a commission I accepted... from a Forest Ranger I know.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: The recent issues with The Withering have occupied a lot of manpower, though I don't know much about the details...

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: So jobs like "handling fierce animals" fell upon me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's why.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Thank you very much for your help! Here's your payment.

response.speaker: Santon
response.text: Really? I wish I could have seen that for myself.
